name: Southwest Rivers Headwaters Fund
summary: NFWF grants to restore, protect and enhance aquatic and riparian species and habitats in the Rio Grande and Colorado River headwaters. Funds process-based riparian restoration, beaver work, species translocation and invasive fish removal; in the 2026 round, Colorado River projects were limited to Farm Bill technical assistance.

geography.label: Rio Grande and Colorado River headwaters

amount.note: Larger requests are considered case by case.

reporting: Grantees choose reporting metrics from the programme's list in NFWF's Easygrants system.

eligibility.rule: Not an international organization, business or unincorporated individual
Colorado River Focal Area projects are limited to NRCS Farm Bill technical assistance
No ongoing legal-compliance efforts, permit conditions, mitigation or settlement agreements

documents: Project maps or diagrams of on-site work, if applicable
Statement of Litigation, unless a federal, state or local government applicant
Board of Trustees or Directors list, or statement that none exists
GAAP audited financial statements, unless current valid information is already on file
IRS Form 990, unless current valid information is already on file
Single Audit, unless current valid information is already on file

status.quote: 11/20/2025 Southwest Rivers Headwaters 2026 Request for Proposals - CLOSED

deadline.quote: Full Proposal Due Date November 12, 2025, 11:59pm EDT / 9:59pm MDT

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include: local, state, federal, and tribal governments and agencies (e.g., townships, cities, boroughs), special districts (e.g., conservation districts, planning districts, utility districts), non-profit 501(c) organizations, educational institutions.

geography.quote: The Rio Grande Headwaters Focal Area includes the mainstem and headwater tributaries of the Rio Grande in Colorado and northern New Mexico

access.quote: is requesting proposals to restore, protect and enhance aquatic and riparian species of conservation concern and their habitats

window.quote: Full Proposal Due Date November 12, 2025, 11:59pm EDT / 9:59pm MDT

amount.quote: Grant requests should be between $100,000 and $600,000, with larger grant requests being considered on a case-by-case basis.

co_finance_required.quote: Applicants are required to provide at least $1 in non-federal matching funds for every $1 of NFWF grant funds requested.

reporting.quote: has a list of metrics in Easygrants for full proposal applicants to choose from for reporting

effort.quote: Full Proposal Due Date November 12, 2025, 11:59pm EDT / 9:59pm MDT

eligibility.quote: Ineligible applicants include: international organizations, businesses or unincorporated individuals.
Projects located in the Colorado River Focal Area of this RFP must be limited to technical assistance activities in support of NRCS Farm Bill programs.
NFWF funds may not be used to support ongoing efforts to comply with legal requirements, including permit conditions, mitigation and settlement agreements.

co_finance.quote: Applicants are required to provide at least $1 in non-federal matching funds for every $1 of NFWF grant funds requested. Eligible matching sources can include cash, in-kind donations, and/or volunteer labor which are directly related to the project proposed for funding.

documents.quote: In addition to the Mapping Tool, please submit maps and/or diagrams of on-site work proposed, if applicable.

Statement of Litigation Yes Template provided in Easygrants online application "Uploads" section. Federal, state, and local government applicants are not required to complete this section. Board of Trustees or Directors Yes Provide a list of members. If your organization is not a nonprofit and does not have a Board, upload a document stating that none exists.
